_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for SRF (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment-driven: each segment's revenue grows and earns an EBITDA margin (segment EBIT + segment depreciation). Group EBITDA = sum of segments less unallocated corporate costs and forex hedge losses (Screener basis). Valued on sum of the parts (EV/EBITDA by segment), as the street does.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments._why: FY27: H1 +25% (refrigerant volumes and prices); management guides 15-20%, 'towards the higher end'. We take 19%: H2 only +14% against a strong Q4FY26 refrigerant season and soft specialty. FY28: +12% because calendar 2027 is a 'free year' before India's HFC quotas, so new capacity can sell and prices may soften; fluoropolymers (PVDF, Chemours FEP/FKM) start to ramp. FY29: +16% as HFOs (Odisha, Q4FY28) and fluoropolymers run for a full year.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 35.7% in FY26 (EBIT 29.1%); ~32.6% in H1FY27 as specialty prices fell under Chinese overcapacity and raw-material/freight costs rose. We assume no return to FY26's peak: 32.8% / 32% / 33%.

segments.name: Performance Films & Foil
segments._why: H1FY27 +46%: the Middle East war shut rival plants, customers panic-bought and polymer prices jumped. We assume H2 +15% and only +2% in FY28 as prices normalise; FY29 +8% from capacitor film, BOPA (Sep-2027), thick BOPET and foil.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 13.2% in FY26 (EBIT 8.8%); H1FY27 ~16.5% including a one-off inventory gain in Q1 (EBIT 17.3%, management: 'an aberration'), Q2 EBIT back to 9.7%. We assume 12.5% in H2 and 13.5-14% after.

segments.name: Technical Textiles
segments._why: H1FY27 +26% (belting exports after US tariff cuts, nylon tyre cord, quality-control order on industrial yarn); H2 assumed +8%. Mature business: ~5% a year after.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 13.4% in FY26; ~17.6% in H1FY27 including inventory gains. 14% from FY28 (FY22-26 average ~15%).

_unallocLabel: Unallocated corporate costs and forex hedge losses (reported EBITDA below sum of segments)
_unallocWhy: FY26: ₹434 cr = ₹188 cr forex losses on long-dated export hedges + ₹246 cr corporate costs. H1FY27: ₹193 cr, of which ₹165 cr forex. FY27E includes the H1 forex loss; FY28-29E assume corporate costs only (~₹150 cr) and no further hedge losses.
_capexWhy: FY27 guided ~₹2,500 cr; FY28 carries most of the ₹2,300 cr Odisha HFO plant, the ₹600 cr battery-foil plant (phase I), BOPA and thick-film lines; Axis expects >₹2,500 cr a year. FY26 actual ₹1,717 cr.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹852 cr ≈ 4.6% of average gross block; H1FY27 ₹452 cr.
_treasuryWhy: Net debt, so no treasury income; other income entered separately.
_otherIncomeWhy: FY26 other income ₹107 cr before the ₹85 cr Labour Codes exceptional charge; H1FY27 ₹59 cr.
_interestWhy: FY26 ₹278 cr; H1FY27 ₹140 cr; gross debt ~₹5,200 cr at Sep-26 and rising with the capex cycle.
_taxWhy: H1FY27 ~23%; FY26 27% included the exceptional charge; normal ~25%.

dcf._betaWhy: Cyclical chemicals and films; market-like sensitivity.
dcf._tgWhy: Long-run demand for refrigerants, fluoropolymers and films tracks industrial growth; 6% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: ≈ India nominal GDP less some maturity of HFCs (phase-down) offset by HFOs and fluoropolymers.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex intensity falls from ~10-12% of revenue to ~6% once the HFO / fluoropolymer cycle is done.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Refrigerant prices hold through the 2027 'free year' and India's 2028 quota freeze; specialty volumes and prices recover with new agro and pharma molecules; HFOs and fluoropolymers ramp on time; films keep a ~14% EBITDA margin.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: HFC prices fall as new capacity sells in 2027; Chinese overcapacity keeps specialty prices down; HFO volumes slip into FY30; films margins revert to the FY24-25 trough.

parts.name: Chemicals
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E EBITDA (½ FY28E + ½ FY29E) × EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Street 15-23x (Kotak 15x, PL 18x, ICICI Direct 20x, Nuvama 20x, MOSL 23x). 20x ≈ half fluorochemicals (Navin Fluorine ~34x, quota-protected) and half specialty (PI Industries ~16x, under Chinese price pressure).

parts.name: Performance Films & Foil
parts.note: Street 8-11x; listed film makers trade at 4-7x (Cosmo First 6.9x, Uflex 5.5x, Polyplex 4.1x). 7x = a small premium for SRF's value-added films and foil.

parts.name: Technical Textiles
parts.note: Street 4-11x (ICICI Direct 4x, PL 6x, MOSL 11x). Mature, import-exposed business: 6x.

parts.name: Less: corporate costs
parts.note: Head-office costs not in any segment are real costs; valued at the blended multiple of the businesses (~16x). Most brokers leave this out, which flatters their SOTP by ~₹80 a share.

parts.name: Less: net debt at Sep-27E
parts.metricLabel: Net debt at the target date (½ Mar-27E + ½ Mar-28E)
parts.note: Model forecast: borrowings less cash and investments.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values SRF: every broker we found with a disclosed method except Elara uses segment EV/EBITDA (Kotak, PL, ICICI Direct, Nuvama, MOSL). The four businesses have very different growth and returns, so each needs its own multiple.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: SRF's one-year-forward P/E has a median of ~36x since 2019; Indian chemical stocks have since de-rated ~20-25% (PI Industries 29x trailing vs a 38x five-year median). 36x × 0.78 ≈ 28x.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 6%. Heavy capex keeps free cash flow low for three years.
